turns.t: Good morning. I'm Pauline, Mia's foster carer. We're here for her twelve-month jabs, and I've got her red book.
Lovely, I'm Nurse Priya, and I'll give the jabs after the doctor's had a look. Hello, Mia! ~
Good morning. Let me just ask a few questions before we vaccinate. How's Mia been this week? ~
She's had a snuffly nose since Monday, but she's feeding well and playing.
Any fever or temperature?
No, I've checked every morning. Never above normal.
Any vomiting or diarrhoea?
No, nothing like that.
Does Mia have any allergies, including to foods?
Egg. She came out in hives and was sick after a bit of scrambled egg at her last foster home, so they told me to be careful.
Thank you, that's important, and it's fine for the jabs we're giving, we'll check. Any other history?
Eczema, on her cheeks and the backs of her knees. It's mild.
Doctor, I've got the vaccine record, Mia's had her eight-week and sixteen-week ones, all on time. ~
Excellent. Let me listen to her chest, and look in her ears, given the cold. ~
She's fine with that.
Her chest is clear, and ears are both normal. The nose is just a bit runny. I can't rule out a brewing ear infection on that left side, but there's no sign yet.
Does that mean we can't vaccinate? ~
No, a mild cold without a fever is fine. Egg allergy is also not a problem for these vaccines. I'm happy to go ahead. ~
Oh good. ~
Today, Mia's having the MMR, the Hib/MenC, the pneumococcal booster, and the meningitis B booster. ~
That's a lot of needles. ~
Four, but quick, and Priya's very good. I'd like to arrange for you to wait fifteen minutes in the waiting room afterwards, so we can check she's well.
Of course. ~
Mia, look at the bubbles, can you see them?
Ooh! Ba ba ba. ~
Waaaah! ~
All done, doctor. She was brilliant. ~
Well done, Mia. Pauline, she may be grumpy and a bit warm for a day or two, and she may have a sore leg.
Can I give her something for it? ~
If she's very upset or hot, you can use infant paracetamol according to the label. ~
Right. ~
If she gets a high temperature, a rash that doesn't fade, or a swollen face, or if she's floppy or won't feed, call 999 or come back straight away.
I will. ~
Her next appointment is at three years, and the practice will send it. I'd like to see her again before then if the ear gets worse.
Thank you, doctor. Thank you, nurse. ~

chief_complaint.value: We're here for her twelve-month jabs

clinical_assessment.assessment: a brewing ear infection on that left side

clinical_actions.description: Wait fifteen minutes in the waiting room after the jabs
Expect grumpiness, mild fever and sore leg; infant paracetamol per label if needed
Safety-net: 999 or return for high temperature, non-fading rash, facial swelling, floppiness or poor feeding
